name: Lightning Bolt
label: Load Records
lede: Two Brians from a Providence art school, a bass strung with banjo strings and a telephone mic taped inside a mask, set up on the floor wherever the crowd happened to be.

eras.title: Three kids and a textile mill
eras.text: Lightning Bolt started at the Rhode Island School of Design as an improvising trio that toured without bothering to record. Its home base was Fort Thunder, a squat-like warehouse in Providence's Olneyville district where Brian Chippendale and friends lived, drew comics, wrestled in costume and put on shows.

years.h: Brian Chippendale meets bass whiz Brian Gibson at RISD
years.p: At the Rhode Island School of Design, drummer Brian Chippendale hears about a new kid who is a whiz on bass. He finds [[Brian Gibson|0aa47f69-47f0-4bf4-a445-8756df8e3d42]], and Lightning Bolt starts in Providence.

years.h: Hisham Bharoocha joins on vocals after the first show
years.p: After Lightning Bolt's first gig, RISD student [[Hisham Bharoocha|724cb291-89dd-4b9f-a968-d7d4531ad66d]] joins on extra percussion and vocals, making it a trio that improvises its sets and tours without recording.

years.h: Brian Chippendale and Mat Brinkman open Fort Thunder
years.p: [[Brian Chippendale|2de5109e-2713-46dd-8de5-f64ee000da49]] and Mat Brinkman take over the second floor of a pre-Civil War textile mill in Olneyville. Fort Thunder becomes home, studio and venue for Providence's noise and comics underground.
years.xp:
The original residents were Brinkman, Chippendale, Rob Coggeshal and Freddy Jones. Fort Thunder became known for its dense, colorful screen-printed posters, costumed wrestling nights and Halloween mazes, as well as shows.

Its alumni went on to noise bands, alternative comics and galleries: the art collective Forcefield, born there, showed at the 2002 Whitney Biennial.

years.h: Hisham Bharoocha leaves for the band that becomes Black Dice
years.p: Hisham Bharoocha quits Lightning Bolt for another RISD band, soon to be [[Black Dice|d8f9a4bd-ec27-4e29-8b3e-b8bdb62f950e]]. His only released Lightning Bolt track is Revenge, on Load's Repopulation Program compilation.

eras.title: Down on the floor
eras.text: As a duo, Chippendale and Gibson worked out the setup that made them: Gibson's bass tuned like a cello, Chippendale pounding drums and shrieking through a telephone receiver. Load Records talked them into making records, but they never trusted the studio, and the live show stayed the point.

years.h: Load Records' Ben McOsker asks for an album
years.p: Lightning Bolt had never thought about writing songs to record until Ben McOsker, founder of Providence's Load Records, approached Brian Chippendale and Brian Gibson in 1997.

years.h: Lightning Bolt debut: 750 vinyl copies on Load
years.p: Lightning Bolt cut five studio tracks for its debut, threw out four, and swapped in lo-fi live tapes from 1997 and 1998. The vinyl ran to 750 copies.

q: Be super loud and you're all set.
years.h: Guerrilla gigs: Lightning Bolt skips the stage
years.p: Lightning Bolt sets up on the venue floor, not the stage, so the crowd forms a tight circle around Brian Chippendale's kit and Brian Gibson's amps. The band has also played kitchens, sidewalks and parking lots.
years.xp:
Sometimes they started seconds after the opening band finished, before anyone had moved. Chippendale sings through a household telephone receiver, held in his mouth or strapped inside a mask, run through effects and a KMD 8021 Drum Exciter.

Gibson tunes his bass to cello tuning (C G D A), uses banjo strings on the high end, and later went to five strings. Volume, he said, solved most problems.

years.h: Ride the Skies · Load Records
years.p: Lightning Bolt's second album is the first made more or less the normal way, in a studio rather than pieced together from live tapes.

years.h: Fort Thunder evicted, mill razed for a supermarket lot
years.p: After two years of protests and court challenges, the Fort Thunder collective is forced out in 2002. Developer Feldco razes the mill for a Shaw's supermarket and Staples parking lot; according to Wikipedia both stores closed soon after opening.

eras.title: Best alarm clock ever
eras.text: The records got clearer, the crowds got bigger and the critics caught up: Metacritic later ranked Lightning Bolt eighth among artists of the 2000s. The band spent the decade crossing oceans, including one trip that ended at immigration, and Chippendale drummed for Björk.

years.h: Wonderful Rainbow · Load No. 41
years.p: Recorded in Providence and Costa Mesa with Dave Auchenbach, Wonderful Rainbow is Lightning Bolt's catchiest record. Pitchfork later ranked it No. 157 of the 2000s, and it's in 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.

years.h: The Power of Salad: the Lightning Bolt DVD
years.p: Peter Glantz and Nick Noe direct The Power of Salad, a DVD film about Lightning Bolt.

q: Best alarm clock I've ever had.
years.h: Lightning Bolt plays John Peel's doorstep at noon at ATP
years.p: At All Tomorrow's Parties in 2004, Lightning Bolt set up at noon on the doorstep of DJ [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]]'s chalet. Next door was [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] of [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]] and [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]].
years.xp: ATP housed its bands in holiday-camp chalets, so a Lightning Bolt guerrilla set could happen anywhere. Peel died that October.

years.h: Frenzy, the lost improv album, is promised and never comes
years.p: A 2004 post on Lightning Bolt's website said an improvised album called Frenzy was in the works at Load, due at the end of summer. It never came out.

years.h: Hypermagic Mountain, cut straight to DAT in a house
years.p: Lightning Bolt recorded Hypermagic Mountain between May 29 and June 21, 2005, half in a studio and half in a Providence house, straight to 2-track DAT. Metacritic ranked it fifth among 2005's albums.
years.xp: Brian Chippendale made the cover art first; the title came after. Engineer Dave Auchenbach captured the house sessions with no multitrack at all. Alternative Press gave it five stars and NME 9/10, while Pitchfork's Brandon Stosuy called it the band's most well-oiled album.

years.h: Deported from Japan days after landing
years.p: Coming from a UK tour, Lightning Bolt is detained on arrival in Japan for lacking work permits. The appeal is rejected after 48 hours, and the band is sent home.

years.h: Brian Chippendale drums on Björk's Volta
years.p: [[Björk|87c5dedd-371d-4a53-9f7f-80522fb7f3cb]] brings Brian Chippendale in to drum on her 2007 album Volta, and again on a 2008 charity single.

years.h: 77 Boadrum: two Lightning Bolt alumni among 77 drummers
years.p: At the [[Boredoms|0798d15b-64e2-499f-9969-70167b1d8617]]' 77 Boadrum in Brooklyn on 7/7/07, Brian Chippendale plays drummer No. 77, and ex-member Hisham Bharoocha is musical director.

years.h: Earthly Delights, the last album on Load
years.p: Lightning Bolt's fifth album is its last full-length for Load Records and the last for almost six years.

eras.title: Comics, video games and a cleaner signal
eras.text: Lightning Bolt went quiet on record while both members built big second careers: Chippendale in comics and art, Gibson designing games at Harmonix and then his own studio. When the band came back, it came back on Thrill Jockey and, for the first time, you could hear everything.

years.h: Metacritic ranks Lightning Bolt eighth among 2000s artists
years.p: Metacritic's Artists of the Decade 2000–09 puts the Providence noise duo at No. 8.

years.h: Brian Chippendale's If 'n Oof and a Brooklyn show
years.p: Brian Chippendale publishes the comic If 'n Oof in 2010 and shows art in "Fruiting Bodies" at Cinders Gallery, Brooklyn, that June. Ninja and Maggots came before; Puke Force follows in 2016.

years.h: Oblivion Hunter EP: 2008 leftovers on Load
years.p: Lightning Bolt's first EP collects unreleased material recorded in 2008.

years.h: Fantasy Empire, Lightning Bolt's Thrill Jockey debut
years.p: Lightning Bolt's first album on Thrill Jockey streams on NPR's First Listen on March 9, 2015. NPR's writeup praises a clarity and fidelity the band's earlier records never had.
years.xp: The nine songs end with the 11-minute Snow White (& The 7 Dwarves Fans). Metacritic scored it 84.

years.h: Brian Gibson quits Harmonix to co-found Drool
years.p: After working as a lead artist at Harmonix since 2001, Brian Gibson leaves in summer 2015 to start the game studio Drool with Marc Flury.

years.h: Brian Gibson's Thumper, a rhythm-violence game
years.p: Drool releases Thumper, with art and music by Brian Gibson, to critical acclaim.

years.h: Rolling Stone ranks Brian Chippendale No. 91 drummer ever
years.p: Rolling Stone's 100 Greatest Drummers of All Time puts Brian Chippendale at No. 91.

eras.title: Back, and still loud
eras.text: Lightning Bolt's seventh album arrived after four more years, with song titles as absurd as ever. Chippendale kept side projects going, including a duo with Ty Segall.

years.h: Sonic Citadel, closing with Van Halen 2049
years.p: Lightning Bolt's second Thrill Jockey album runs 11 songs, from Blow to the Head to USA Is a Psycho and Van Halen 2049.

years.h: Wasted Shirt: Brian Chippendale and Ty Segall's Fungus II
years.p: Brian Chippendale and [[Ty Segall|07a17571-81fc-4cf8-a634-98f0d926d313]] release Fungus II as the duo Wasted Shirt.
